extracted.intended_audience: museums, museum-affiliated nonprofit organizations, and eligible government entities preparing applications for the IMLS Museums for America FY2023 grant program
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a complete Museums for America (MFA-FY23) grant application to IMLS that aligns with program goals, meets eligibility and cost-share requirements, and follows all formatting, content, and supporting-document instructions in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program alignment to IMLS agency goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Each award that IMLS makes through Museums for America will align with one of the agency-level goals and one associated objective and contribute meaningfully to program and agency-level goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must identify clearly in the Narrative which program goal/project category and associated objective(s) their project will address (see Section A2). Choice of program goal informs project category (Lifelong Learning, Community Engagement, Collections Stewardship and Access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Museums for America program goals and objectives (selection guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program goals: (1) Lifelong Learning (objectives: support public/adult/family/early childhood programs; support exhibitions/interpretation/digital media; support in-school and out-of-school programs); (2) Community Engagement (objectives: audience research/evaluation/outreach; community-driven exhibitions/programs; community-focused planning and civic engagement); (3) Collections Stewardship and Access (objectives: cataloging/inventory/registration/collections planning; conservation/environmental improvement/rehousing/conservation surveys/treatment; database/digital asset management/digitization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align proposed project with one of these three goals and one or more associated objectives and reference that alignment in the Narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Museums for America uses four performance measures: Effectiveness, Efficiency, Quality, and Timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must describe how they will monitor and assess performance for their overall project from the perspectives of these four measures (see Section D2c Item 8). For each measure, identify data to collect, sources, methods, and schedule; use the two-page Performance Measurement Plan template or similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness (performance measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness: The extent to which activities contribute to achieving the intended results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Performance Measurement Plan, state what data will demonstrate contribution to intended results and how you will collect/assess it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency (performance measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency: How well resources (e.g., funds, expertise, time) are used and costs are minimized while generating maximum value for the target group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe metrics and methods to track resource use and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality (performance measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality: How well the activities meet the requirements and expectations of the target group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify measures (surveys, observations, expert review) that capture whether activities meet target group needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (performance measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness: The extent to which each task/activity is completed within the timeframe proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Schedule of Completion and progress tracking to demonstrate adherence to timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with authorizing statute and federal regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and recipients must comply with the IMLS authorizing statute (20 U.S.C. § 9101 et seq.; § 9173) and applicable regulations (45 C.F.R. Chapter XI; 2 C.F.R. part 200 Uniform Guidance; IMLS-specific 2 C.F.R. part 3187).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must follow the IMLS regulations in effect at the time of award and the Uniform Guidance requirements for administrative, cost, and audit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity/non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS-funded programs do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, or age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact CivilRights@imls.gov for further information; ensure your project does not discriminate and complies with civil rights obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding request limits and award parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected individual award amounts: $5,000 - $250,000; IMLS expects to award $21,699,000 total; anticipated number of awards is 120; projects must begin September 1, 2023 and run one to three years (period of performance September 1, 2023 - August 31, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If total federal request (direct + indirect) is less than $5,000 or greater than $250,000, the application will be rejected. Projects must have start date Sept 1, 2023. IMLS is not bound by the estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements (three-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Museums for America, an organization must (1) be a unit of State, local, or tribal government or a private nonprofit with tax-exempt status under the Internal Revenue Code; (2) be located in one of the listed U.S. jurisdictions (50 States, DC, territories, and certain freely associated states); and (3) qualify as a museum (professional staff, organized on a permanent basis for educational/cultural/aesthetic purposes; owns/uses tangible objects; cares for and exhibits them to the public on a regular basis) or be an eligible agency applying on behalf of a museum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'professional staff' = at least one FTE engaged in acquisition/care/exhibition; 'exhibit to the general public' generally = at least 120 days/year. See 2 C.F.R. § 3187.3 for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of museums within parent organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: A museum within a parent organization may apply on its own behalf only if it can independently fulfill eligibility requirements, functions as a discrete unit, has its own fully segregated and itemized operating budget, and has authority to make the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these conditions cannot be met, the museum must apply through its parent organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of nonprofit organizations affiliated with a museum
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprofit affiliated with a museum may be eligible if it demonstrates ability to administer the project and ensure compliance; the applicant must submit an agreement from the museum detailing activities and binding the museum to statements and assurances in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS may request documentation; ensure clear agreements and administrative capacity are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share (match) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide non-federal funds in an amount equal to or greater than the federal award (1:1 cost share).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost share must appear in the project budget and be defensible; applications lacking at least 1:1 cost share will be rejected from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications and distinct projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants may submit multiple applications for support of separate and distinct projects under this announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting to this program does not preclude applying to other IMLS programs; ensure projects are distinct and independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and lead applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more eligible institutions collaborate, one must meet all eligibility requirements, serve as lead applicant, and administer the award; the lead will be programmatically, fiscally, and legally responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify roles, responsibilities, and fiscal relationships in application and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application method and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must apply electronically through Grants.gov Workspace or a Grants.gov system-to-system solution using Funding Opportunity Number MFA-FY23; all materials must be received through Grants.gov by 11:59 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on November 15, 2022. Late applications will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not wait to register; allow weeks for Grants.gov and SAM registration. Audio/paper needs contact info provided for accommodation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include all Required Documents and Conditionally Required Documents listed in the Table of Application Components; missing required or conditionally required documents will render the application incomplete and may be rejected (see 2 C.F.R. § 3187.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided table as a checklist; required items include SF-424S, IMLS Supplementary Information Form (including Abstract), IMLS Museum Program Information Form, Organizational Profile, Strategic Plan Summary, Narrative (7 pages max), Schedule of Completion, Performance Measurement Plan (2 pages max), IMLS Budget Form, Budget Justification, List of Key Project Staff, Resumes, plus any conditionally required docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document format, naming, page limits, and attachment order
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for forms created in Grants.gov, all components must be PDF documents. Page limits are enforced (additional pages removed). File names must use only the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen, space, period. Attach components in the sequence listed in the table; use available attachment spaces first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified file names (e.g., Narrative.pdf, Budget.pdf). Reviewers will not see removed over-limit pages; improper filenames may cause rejection by Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative requirements (format and organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative: limit to seven numbered pages; be clear and concise with minimal technical jargon; include references to Supporting Documents; organization must follow section headings: Project Justification, Project Work Plan, Project Results; include organization name at top of each page; use at least 0.5-inch margins and font size of at least eleven points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS will remove additional pages. The Narrative should consider the chosen Museums for America goal/objective(s) and the review criteria (see Section E1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Justification content
rubrics_metrics.description: In Project Justification, address: which program goal/project category and objective(s) will your project address; how project advances institution's strategic plan; the need/problem/challenge addressed and how it was identified using reliable data; who is the target group and how they were involved in planning (identify numbers if possible); who are the ultimate beneficiaries (identify numbers if reliable or describe characteristics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use demographic information, economic circumstances, condition assessments, and other relevant data from reliable sources to define need and scope. Be explicit about target groups vs beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Work Plan content
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe specific activities and their sequence; risks and mitigation strategies; who will plan/implement/manage the project; time, financial, personnel, and other resources needed; and how progress will be tracked toward intended results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail for reviewers to assess feasibility and management; align tasks to schedule and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Results content
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe intended results and how they address the need from dual perspectives of advancing knowledge/understanding and ensuring federal investment generates benefits to society; how knowledge/skills/behaviors/attitudes of target group will change; what products will result; sustainability beyond period of performance; and for Collections projects, how care/condition/management/access/use of collections/data will improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurable or defensible estimates of numbers served when possible; describe products and long-term sustainment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Completion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule of Completion should reflect each major activity from the Narrative and project dates and show when each major activity will start and end; no longer than one page per project year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided sample schedule format; Schedule may be published online if funded (do not include sensitive info).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Measurement Plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit to two pages and show how performance will be monitored/assessed from perspectives of Effectiveness, Efficiency, Quality, and Timeliness. For each measure, identify what data will be collected, source, method, and schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fillable chart is provided as a sample; include defensible data collection plans and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMLS Budget Form and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must download and complete the current IMLS Budget Form and provide a Budget Justification that identifies each expense and shows the method of cost computation used to determine each dollar amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide vendor quotes or price lists as Supporting Documents when appropriate; detail calculation methods for travel, supplies, subawards/contracts, student support, indirect costs, and other costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Key Project Staff and Resumes requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a one-page list of only staff/consultants essential to project success (include Project Director). Provide resumes (two pages max each) for essential personnel; if not identified by deadline, provide position descriptions instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resumes must be combined into a single PDF. Do not list all staff—only key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionally required documents (when applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide specific documents depending on circumstances: Proof of private nonprofit status (IRS letter) if applying as private nonprofit; Final Federally Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement if using negotiated indirect rate; Digital Products Plan if proposing digital content; Detailed condition reports/conservation treatment proposals if proposing conservation treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide a Conditionally Required Document when applicable will result in an incomplete application and possible rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan structure and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants proposing digital products must submit a two-page Digital Products Plan organized to address Type, Availability, Access, and Sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS expects use of appropriate standards; FADGI resources are recommended. The plan will be scrutinized by staff and peer reviewers and affect funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe digital content/resources/assets to be created or collected, quantities, digital file formats, accompanying metadata, and relevant standards; for software, specify programming languages, platforms, frameworks, and rationale for choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient technical detail for reviewers to assess preservation and reuse potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how digital products will be made openly available (as appropriate), the delivery strategy (open online, restricted, kiosks, programs), and underlying hardware/software platforms; identify and explain any limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS encourages making works widely available and expects publications resulting from awards to be available without charge. Describe platforms (repositories, IIIF, browser accessibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Access and licensing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify rights asserted and limitations; state licensing (e.g., Creative Commons); note that IMLS reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to reproduce/use works for federal purposes; IMLS expects recipients to release files under open-source licenses when possible and distribute work products free or at cost unless IMLS approves otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe handling of privacy and cultural sensitivities and how you will address them (e.g., access controls, restricted metadata, community permissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans for preserving and maintaining digital products during and after the award, including appropriate curation horizons for different product types, storage systems, shared repositories, technical documentation, migration planning, and organizational funding commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between long-lived products needing permanent preservation and short/medium-lived materials; indicate institutional commitments and repositories for long-term access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation survey guidance — General Conservation Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: General Conservation Survey should describe conditions, identify conservation problems, and suggest future conservation activities in general terms; report should include executive summary, general info about museum, goals of survey, overview of collections/condition/policies, descriptions of building/facilities/exhibition/storage areas, climate control/environmental conditions, staffing/training needs, and prioritized recommendations for future conservation care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general survey is often the first step in collections conservation and should form the basis of a long-range conservation plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation survey guidance — Detailed Conservation Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed conservation survey is an item-by-item examination by a conservation professional producing condition reports that identify condition, treatment priority, and cost/method of treatment; a detailed survey should precede any IMLS grant request to fund treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed surveys to establish treatment priorities and necessary resources/time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation survey guidance — Environmental Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: An environmental survey assesses museum environmental conditions (temperature, relative humidity, light) and is conducted by a conservation professional; funds may be used to survey exhibition, storage, and other collection spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental surveys help identify problems, set priorities for improvements, design solutions, develop monitoring programs, and map collections (for living plants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-federal entities must follow IMLS conflict of interest policies: maintain written standards of conduct covering conflicts and performance of employees engaged in selection/award/administration of subawards and contracts; employees may not participate in selection/award/administration if they have a real or apparent conflict (financial or other tangible benefit); officers/employees/agents must not solicit/accept gratuities from subrecipients/contractors; organizational conflicts of interest must also be covered when parent/affiliate/subsidiary relationships exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any potential conflict in writing immediately to an IMLS Program Officer (or pass-through entity if subrecipient/contractor). Ensure written standards and disclosure practices are in place for subawards and contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords in Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Abstract block, list from one to eight keywords that best characterize the project, choosing from the provided keyword list; separate keywords with commas. IMLS may use these in compilations and search tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select no more than eight keywords and choose terms that accurately reflect project focus (e.g., Collections Care, Community Engagement, Digital Preservation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirements (UEI, SAM, Grants.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, applicants must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), a current and active SAM registration, and an active Grants.gov registration with an approved Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow several weeks to complete registrations; check registrations well in advance of the deadline. Subrecipients also must have UEIs before receiving subawards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer verification and potential website review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may choose to visit the applicant organization's website listed on the SF-424S form as part of application review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure website content is consistent with the application and does not include sensitive/confidential information that should not be public if funded.
